source_text: Cum secundum sententiam Evangelii, ex fructibus suis arbor debeat agnosci, hic audiendus putetur, qui dicit bonum esse coniugium, de quo nihil aliud quam malum prodire definite
pass_a_gloss: When/with according-to position of-the-Gospel, from fruits his-own tree debeat to-be-recognized, here to-be-heard let-him-be-thought, who he-says good to-be marriage, about/from whither nothing other than/which evil to-come-forth you-define.

lemmas.lexica: LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: Since, according to the Gospel’s judgment, a tree should be recognized by its fruits (Matthew 7:16–18), should this man be listened to when he says that marriage is good, yet declares that nothing but evil comes from it?

choices.why: Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

bible_refs.note: Linked from Julian's wording or a clear allusion in the excerpt.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
